item.title: Brandon Aiyuk returns to 49ers facility, speaks to media in Santa Clara
item.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk warms up before an NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Oct. 6, 2024. (Jed Jacobsohn/AP) Disgruntled San Francisco 49ers star wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is back in Santa Clara, turning an otherwise standard Friday practice day for the team into a surreal scene. Ahead of a scheduled 3 p.m. meeting, the wide receiver appeared at the team's business offices, which are about a tenth of a mile west of Levi's Stadium and half a mile from the team's practice facility. Aiyuk arrived in a black van along with his new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, with both giving brief statements to the throng of reporters stationed in front of the office. Drew Rosenhaus and Brandon Aiyuk stop and briefly address the media before his meeting with #49ers, which is about to begin. https://t.co/A3ClTXIce1 - Nick Wagoner (@nwagoner) November 6, 2026 "Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team. Fortunately, he's feeling good physically; he's healthy, he's ready to get back to work," Rosenhaus said. "Don't really have any comment about where he's going to play. We'll keep that between us and the Niners. But obviously, we're here with all the right intentions." With a news helicopter circling above the gathering, Aiyuk told reporters it was "nice to see y'all" before he said: "I'm feeling great, feeling healthy. A long recovery process, long rehab process, but I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League." As Aiyuk and Rosenhaus began to walk into the 49ers offices, the former two-time 1,000-yard receiver repeated his last line to a reporter who shouted a question at him. Rosenhaus declined most other inquiries, saying they may have a few more comments after the meeting, but when California Post reporter Evan Webeck asked about Aiyuk's outstanding arrest warrant, Rosenhaus looked back over his shoulder and said, "We're working on that." Throughout Friday, Santa Clara police cars were spotted around the 49ers team facilities, something team beat reporters noted was uncommon for a practice day. The department put out a warrant for Aiyuk's arrest in June , stemming from Aiyuk posting a video of himself driving up to 104 mph on city streets last December. Aiyuk is appearing at the 49ers facility as part of his attempt to return to the NFL. He's expected to have to negotiate with the 49ers over a reported $13 million that the NFL says he owes the team, money stemming from the signing bonus he got when he signed a four-year, $120 million extension in 2024. Aiyuk hasn't played a game in more than two years since going down with a knee injury in October 2024 and has been on the reserve/left squad list after leaving the Niners late last season. He fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until he recently hired Rosenhaus. item.title: Green Bay Packers guard reveals how he’s adjusting to new role in the offensive line
item.description: The Green Bay Packers made an unexpected lineup decision in Week 8, assigning Laken Tomlinson to right guard despite the veteran having started at that position just once during his 12-year NFL career. Tomlinson said he is adjusting well to the new position, although the switch proved more challenging last week because of the condensed schedule and limited practice opportunities. “I mean, it’s definitely a challenge, especially last week,” Tomlinson shared. Green Bay’s Thursday night game in Week 8 left little room for a proper practice session, forcing Tomlinson to adjust to right guard with limited work alongside his teammates. This week’s longer preparation window, however, gives him more time to get comfortable on the right side of the offensive line. Laken Tomlinson with the Green Bay Packers Dec 8, 2024; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Seattle Seahawks guard Laken Tomlinson (70) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images “This week, especially going into the long weekend, I had some extra time to kind of just like go over some stuff on my own. Work on my technique and just work on flipping things technique-wise, and having these two days of practice. So definitely a lot more comfortable now,” the Packers veteran remarked. Tomlinson has logged 11,131 career snaps at left guard, compared with just 131 at right guard following his Week 8 start. Despite his limited experience on the opposite side, the Packers’ coaching staff felt his performance was too strong to take him out of the lineup. item.title: Fear the Reaper
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 07: Mason Miller #22 of the San Diego Padres delivers the pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the seventh inning in game four of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on October 07, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Mason Miller It took quite a haul to bring Miller to San Diego. The Friars traded for the elite closer at the 2025 Deadline, shipping off No. 3 overall prospect Leo De Vries in a blockbuster deal. It’s turned out well for the Padres thus far. Miller was dominant down the stretch in 2025, acting as a setup man behind former closer Robert Suarez. In 23 1/3 innings with the Friars, Miller allowed just two runs (0.77 ERA). Overall Grade: A Even though it didn’t seem possible, he looked even better in 2026. Miller posted a 1.67 ERA over 70 innings of work. In that time, he struck out a ridiculous 129 batters with a 0.90 WHIP and .152 opponent batting average. Miller set a Padres’ franchise record for consecutive scoreless innings with 34 2/3 frames. It’s the eighth-longest scoreless streak by a reliever in MLB history. Miller had just one problem, knocking his grade from an A+ to an A. He often couldn’t throw his fastball for a strike. It didn’t happen terribly often, but when it rained it poured. Miller’s tantalizing stuff was good enough to get him out of jams, but he walked 26 batters in the season. May was a particularly odd month for the elite closer, with Miller notching a 1.24 WHIP (more than 0.30 points over his season mark). Even still, Miller was one of the best relief pitchers in baseball. The right-hander was named a finalist for the NL Reliever of the Year Award alongside Jhoan Duran and Trevor Megill. Miller is the obvious frontrunner for the award, though Duran and Megill are both phenomenal in their own right. With Jason Adam and Adrian Morejon potentially departing, Miller will be one of the Padres’ most important arms in the coming season.

item.title: Cowboys’ Dak Prescott Calls Out George Pickens Trade Speculation: ‘People Say a Lot of Things I Don’t Believe’
item.description: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens has recorded 39 receptions for 533 yards and two touchdowns through eight games this season. He continues to anchor the team’s passing attack with a 13.67-yard average per catch. Dallas’ 3-5 start has fueled trade speculation, but Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb have publicly supported Pickens and the Cowboys’ receiving group. Dak Prescott backs George Pickens against recent trade rumors Prescott dismissed suggestions that Dallas should move Pickens. The quarterback described the receiver as a dependable teammate who accepts a variety of assignments, including blocking and running routes designed to create opportunities for others. Dallas Cowboys receiver George Pickens during NFC practice at the NFL Flag Fieldhouse at Moscone Center South Building. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images “George is a great teammate. And I say that in the sense of, he’s gonna do whatever is asked, he’s gonna do whatever is called. If it’s to go block, if it’s to just go run a guy off, he’s gonna do that. He believes in just doing the right thing, and the ball will come his way at times. And so, that’s not on George,” Prescott said , according to Jon Machota’s post. The comments came after Dallas fell to 3-5. Pickens’ contract situation has created discussion, but his production gives the Cowboys a reason to keep him. His 533 receiving yards rank among the league’s top receiver totals, highlighted by a standout 134-yard, two-touchdown performance against Green Bay in Week 4. Lamb has also rejected the trade talk. He said his accomplishments have been connected to Pickens’ work. Their different roles give Prescott two established targets. Dallas added Pickens to a group built around Lamb. Pickens wins outside and on contested catches, and Lamb creates separation from the slot. Both give Prescott reliable options. Pickens is approaching the end of his rookie contract. Dallas also must plan for cornerback Joey Porter Jr., and reporter Nick Harris said the team has begun discussing those decisions. A mock proposal linked Pickens to Kansas City for Xavier Worthy and draft picks, but that scenario was not an actual reported negotiation. The trade proposal report described it as hypothetical. The Cowboys must now weigh their current struggles against the long-term value of keeping an established star receiver like Pickens. Prescott’s defense gives Dallas a clear football position. Pickens is producing, his teammates trust him, and the offense has invested in his role beside Lamb. Trading him would add another challenge to the Cowboys’ offense. item.title: Draymond Green’s Stats Look Ugly, But His Importance To The Warriors Remains Unchanged
item.description: Mandatory Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green is a future Hall of Famer, but you wouldn’t know it by just looking at his stats. Green’s raw numbers have never shown his true value to the Warriors, but they have been particularly bad in this 2026-27 season. Green is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists, 0.9 steals, and 0.9 blocks per game for the Warriors, while shooting 38.1% from the field and 22.2% from beyond the arc. Calling these ugly would be an understatement. Green has scored 21 points on 21 field goal attempts while committing 22 turnovers and 18 fouls. The Warriors have actually also been better when the 36-year-old has been off the court to this point. According to PBP Stats , they have a +7.9 net rating without him and a +2.1 net rating with him. Despite all this, though, Green’s importance to the Warriors was once again on display against the Miami Heat on Thursday. He started at center and was up against a frontcourt duo of Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo . The Warriors should have gotten crushed inside, but won the points in the paint battle 50-32. Green notably did a fabulous job guarding Antetokounmpo, who finished with just 20 points (7-13 FG), 14 rebounds, and four assists. Draymond is taking the challenge of guarding Giannis and Bam head on and he is holding his own. — Joe Viray (@JoeVirayNBA) November 6, 2026 There aren’t many players in the NBA who can do what Green pulled off against the Heat. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr was asked about his performance postgame and sang his praises. “I thought Draymond was brilliant guarding Giannis,” Kerr said. “He stayed in front. We really didn’t let Giannis get too many buckets in the paint, which is always the key. You want to build a wall in front of him and make him score over the top, which he was doing in the first half. “But you live with those buckets,” Kerr continued. “And I think Dray does as good a job on him as anybody possibly can, just playing the angles, using his strength to keep him out of the paint and battling him without fouling. So, he did a great job on that end and then really distributed the ball well at the other end.” Green finished with two points (1-3 FG), five rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, and one block as the Warriors beat the Heat 120-100. While he was showered with praise from all corners for keeping Antetokounmpo in check, he made it clear postgame he couldn’t have done it by himself. “No one in this league is stopping Giannis one-on-one,” Green said. “If your teammates are not in gaps, is not building the wall when he’s coming downhill, you stand no chance. He joined Jim Harbaugh’s staff to guide Justin Herbert’s unit, but he has faced major challenges in reaching the team’s desired offensive success. Due to a lack of consistency on the field and rising pressure, the coaching staff decided to make a strategic shift. item.title: Recovery vs. Reconstruction: The challenge that lies ahead for Juventus
item.description: VIGO, SPAIN - OCTOBER 15: Luciano Spalletti, Giovanni Carnevali of Juventus ahead of the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Real Club Celta and Juventus at Estadio Balaidos on October 15, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Daniele Badolato - Juventus FC/Juventus FC via Getty Images) | Juventus FC via Getty Images When Juventus’ long road back to relevance is discussed — hopefully in a season or two from now — one word will probably dominate that conversation: recovery. For years, that word made sense. We have spent a while recovering from sporting decline, financial excesses, executive upheaval, points deductions, and coaching changes that all add up to the most turbulent period in the club’s modern history. The objective, if someone had of asked us, appeared simple: get back to where we used to be. I think we can all agree, that moment has passed. The evidence now is that this is no longer a recovery project, it is a full-on reconstruction attempt — and this has real implications for what we should expect and how we measure success. It means, bluntly, that we need to change how we think about this Juventus. In general, recovery is about reclaiming something that already existed. It looks a little backwards and says “let’s do that again.” Reconstruction, on the other hand, tends to be more about building something that has not had a previous incarnation. This has a sense of future focus, a greater freedom to it, a possibility of difference (albeit for better or for worse). This distinction is often lost in our game-to-game football discussions, especially when we are seeing one every three or four days. However, during this avalanche of matchdays and standing back from them, I no longer see a struggling giant working towards the return of former glory. I see a new project and I see it has very different ideas about what success might look like. The strongest evidence of this comes from looking beyond results. When we think of progress, we usually focus on league position, Champions League placings, and trophies. Truthfully, I think reconstruction gets measured with less glamorous indicators. Consider the club’s financial direction. Juventus reduced its overall salary expenditure by approximately 15% between 2023 and 2024 as part of a deliberate strategy to lower costs and create a more sustainable model. I’ve scoured the public internets and it seems as though the wage bill fell from nearly €200 million gross in the 2022-23 season to just below €150 million all of a year later. At the same time, the club doubled down on moving away from the finished product, superstar-driven approach that defined the latter parts of the previous decade. (Looking at you, Ronaldo.) item.title: SCOUTING VALENCIA: Should be a breeze in theory, but Valencia at the Mestalla is never easy
item.description: Mexican coach Javier Aguirre is presented as the new manager of Valencia CF at a press conference at the Mestalla stadium in Valencia, on September 28, 2026. (Photo by Jose Miguel Fernandez/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Valencia are on their third coach after just 11 league matches. Carlos Corberán’s dismissal, Óscar Sánchez’s brief spell in charge and Javier Aguirre’s arrival have brought two wins, three draws and six defeats. They have scored eight goals and conceded 17. The lack of goals is their most immediate problem. Valencia have created 10.8 non-penalty expected goals, ranking 17th in La Liga, but scored only six when penalties and own goals are excluded. They are struggling both to create enough and to finish the chances they do get. Umar Sadiq leads the squad with 1.8 npxG and two goals. Hugo Duro and Arnaut Danjuma have yet to score despite chances worth 1.6 and 1.4 npxG respectively. Valencia’s most productive attacking spell came in their seventh and eighth matches, when they averaged 1.85 npxG. They have conceded 14.8 npxG, an average of 1.34 per match, with 14 non-penalty goals allowed. Opponents are scoring roughly in line with the chances Valencia concede. Much of their defending takes place close to home. Their defensive actions occur an average of 30 metres from their own goal line, the deepest figure in La Liga. Their PPDA of 15.8 is also the league’s highest, indicating that opponents are allowed more passes before Valencia intervene outside their own defensive third. The league average is 12.4. That limited pressure is reflected in where matches are played. Valencia account for just 36.4% of final-third passes, the lowest share in the division, and have held the larger share in only two of their 11 games. Across the pitch’s 24 zones, they have controlled five, compared with 11 for their opponents. Possession has offered little relief. Valencia complete 313 open-play passes per match, ranking 15th, and only 21.2% of the passes they receive arrive in the final third. Their passing has generated 9.3 expected threat, the second-lowest total in La Liga. Danjuma leads that measure with 0.97 xT, followed by Pepelu on 0.93 and Luis Rioja on 0.71. Their most-used formation has been 4-4-2, while José Gayà and Justin de Haas are their most frequent passing partnership, exchanging 23 passes. Valencia average 10.3 non-penalty shots per match, each worth 0.10 npxG. Their average shooting distance of 17.8 metres ranks ninth shortest, but the goals have not followed. They have spent almost 64% of their season level and just 10.1% ahead. Aguirre’s task is to give them more ways to move up the pitch and turn those long periods at parity into winning positions. So far, Valencia have spent too much time defending and made too little of their opportunities when they arrive.

item.title: Carson Hocevar Finally Feels NASCAR’s Heat
item.description: HOMESTEAD, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 06: NASCAR Cup Series driver, Carson Hocevar speaks to the media during a press conference at Homestead-Miami Speedway on November 06, 2026 in Homestead, Florida. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty Images There was probably nowhere else Carson Hocevar wanted to be less than the third floor of the media center at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Friday. Of course, Hocevar didn’t really need to be at the site of the final NASCAR Cup Series race of the 2026 season. That’s because he won’t be racing on Sunday. His team, Spire Motorsports, announced earlier in the week that it was suspending the driver of the No. 77 Chevrolet for the season finale. So no one expected Hocevar to be at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Friday. Yet there he was. And judging by his demeanor, there were probably a dozen other places he’d rather have been. It all started the previous Sunday at Martinsville Speedway. During the race, Hocevar, apparently angered by something, brake-checked Team Penske driver Austin Cindric not once, but twice. The result was considerable damage to Cindric’s Ford, forcing him to retire from the event. Shortly after Spire announced its suspension, NASCAR handed Hocevar another helping of consequences, fining him $100,000 and docking him 25 driver points. It was the latest chapter in a season filled with on-track incidents that left crashed cars and angry drivers in their wake. On Thursday, Hocevar released a video on his YouTube channe l. In it, he took responsibility for the actions that put him on the sidelines this weekend. He admitted he was the “bad guy” and appeared genuinely remorseful. FORBES | By Greg Engle Carson Hocevar’s NASCAR Season Ends With A Lesson In Accountability Apparently, taking responsibility for your actions is considerably easier when you’re doing it from the comfort of your own YouTube channel. Friday, when meeting with the media, Hocevar looked like a driver who would much rather have been anywhere else than answering questions about the mess he’d made. But he showed up, and he didn’t shy away from acknowledging that he knew his actions at Martinsville could bring serious consequences. “Probably, you know, before I started hitting the brakes,” Hocevar said when asked when he realized he might face significant punishment. “I knew it was like a possibility for sure. But, you know, I took a percentage risk of that.” In other words, he knew there was a chance the stunt would cost him. He just apparently wasn’t expecting the bill to be quite so large.
